question: Using a suitable property of definite integrals, evaluate $\displaystyle I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$.
explanation:
Step 1: Applying the change-of-argument property
Use the property $\displaystyle \int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$. Here $a=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Thus,
$$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}\,dx$$
Step 2: Simplifying the transformed integrand
Using $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\cos x$ and $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\sin x$,
$$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$$
Step 3: Adding the two equivalent forms
$$2I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}1\,dx$$
Step 4: Evaluating the remaining integral
$$2I=\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Step 5: Obtaining the required value
Therefore, $\boxed{I=\frac{\pi}{4}}$.
